small_guidance:
- Fuse the channel-max reduction into the normalize/clamp kernel: instead of writing the intermediate (N,C,S) tensor and re-reading it, have one program per (N, S-tile) that loops over C computing per-channel mean/invstd (two passes over S) and accumulates the running max across channels in registers, eliminating an entire HBM round-trip on a (128,16,2744) tensor.
- Autotune BLOCK_S over {256, 512, 1024, 2048} with num_warps ∈ {4,8} and num_stages ∈ {2,3}; the current S=2744 is small enough that a persistent-row kernel keeping the (n,c) slice resident pays off.
- Precompute mean/invstd once per (n,c) into a small (N,C) scratch tensor (two tiny kernels) so the max-fused kernel only needs one pass over S per channel rather than three.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a single fused kernel: grid = (N, ceil(S/BLOCK_S)). For each (n, s-tile), loop c=0..C-1; for each channel first compute mean/invstd via two reductions over the full S (cached in shared/registers across tiles is hard, so instead launch a tiny pre-kernel that produces (N,C) mean+invstd tensors), then in the main kernel load x[n,c,s_tile], apply (x*m - mean)*invstd, clamp, *m, and reduce-max into an accumulator over c. Write the final max once. This collapses 3 passes over the (N,C,S) intermediate to 1.
- Also consider fusing the conv epilogue: since Conv3d output is what feeds this, and conv currently isn't custom, profile whether conv dominates — if so, write an im2col-GEMM Conv3d with the multiplier baked into the epilogue bias path; otherwise the norm+clamp+max fusion above is the main lever.
- Use channels-last-ish layout (N, S, C) for the fused kernel so the inner c-loop loads are contiguous across the max reduction, improving coalescing when C=16 fits in a single vector load.
